newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says inflation pressure reasonable.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says inflation pressure reasonable.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said inflation pressures in the British economy remained quite reasonable and that the latest set of data did not make higher interest rates inevitable.
"The inflation pressure in the economy remains quite reasonable," Clarke told a news conference.
Asked if Wednesday's sales and jobless data made a rate hike more likely, he said nothing made any rise in rates in any way inevitable.
"I'm unflinching in my determination to hit that inflation target," Clarke said.
The government has a medium-term target of 2.5 percent for annual underlying inflation. In November, RPIX was 3.3 percent year-on-year.
